correctness.rationale: Every factor has the same distance-quotient intersection numbers; the profile partition is equitable with exact five transition multiplicities. Root visibility separates shells by radius. If mu=2 and k=2lambda+2, each distance shell is equitable and its cardinality follows from the strongly regular parameter relation. Otherwise predecessor counts at arrival (mu!=2) or within-shell counts one round later (mu=2,k!=2lambda+2) distinguish all feasible coordinate-distance profiles. Nonempty final shells give a genuine 2d-1 lower bound. Standalone direct graph tests on 20 constructed examples and all predicted class sizes passed; they corroborate, not replace, the general proof.

value.rationale: The exact dichotomy separates uniform-distance information (2d+1 cells) from full three-level coordinate-profile information (binomial(d+2,2) cells) in every product of arbitrary common-parameter strongly regular graphs. It gives exact sharp refinement depth, all class cardinalities, and a parameter-only trace invariant across possibly nonisomorphic factors, connecting finite-model counting logic with the natural distance-regular/Doob vs non-Hamming structural boundary. This is not a substitution into a known table, since the non-Hamming all-factor partition separation requires a new inductive refinement argument.
